Tucked away quietly in Kalyan West, this restaurant is truly a hidden treasure. From the outside, it looks ordinary, but the moment you walk in, the beautifully crafted interiors simply leave you amazed. The ambience is elegant, warm, and far more luxurious than anything you’d imagine from the exterior.

A close friend recently celebrated his son’s birthday here, and the entire event was handled flawlessly. The staff is extremely polite, cooperative, and genuinely attentive. Their hospitality adds a special touch that makes every moment feel well taken care of.

The food is exceptional — flavourful, fresh, and served with great presentation. If there's one thing you must try, it’s their dimsums. Both veg and non-veg are perfectly prepared and easily among the best in the area.

The restaurant arranged a sort of private table for us, which made it feel special and comfortable for our large gathering. The ambiance has a nice rustic charm, and it felt like the perfect place to sit back, enjoy conversations, and share a hearty meal.

We began with soups – some of us chose the Cream of Tomato, while a few went for the Vegetable Manchow. The Cream of Tomato was spot on with its rich yet balanced sweetness, smooth consistency, a drizzle of cream, and crunchy breadcrumbs to top it off. It was satisfying and flavorful. However, the Manchow soup was a bit of a letdown – while it had plenty of veggies, it was extra spicy and lacked that signature tang and flavor one usually expects. Adding fried noodles made it slightly better, but overall it fell short compared to the tomato soup.

For starters, we tried a variety – cheese balls, honey chilli potatoes, stuffed mushroom tandoori, and peanut chaat. The cheese balls were the highlight, perhaps the best I’ve had, mainly because they were pure cheese without any fillers like corn. Each bite burst with soft, molten cheese wrapped in a crunchy outer layer – a real treat for cheese lovers. The honey chilli potatoes tasted good but were overwhelmingly spicy despite us asking for medium spice. The stuffed mushrooms were generously portioned and very well received – smoky from the tandoor, with a flavorful paneer and veggie filling. On the other hand, the peanut chaat didn’t quite work for us; it had a vinegar-like coating that felt unusual, making the dish more average than enjoyable.

Moving on to the main course, we ordered Malai Kofta, Paneer Butter Masala, and Veg Handi, along with a mix of rotis, naans, and makai roti. The Malai Kofta was outstanding – rich cashew gravy, creamy but not overly sweet, with soft, perfectly cooked koftas that paired wonderfully with the hot rotis. Both the Paneer Butter Masala and Veg Handi were excellent too. The paneer pieces were soft, with ample portions in the creamy orange gravy, and the dish was made exactly as per our request without coriander. The Veg Handi lived up to its name with a mix of beans, carrots, peas, and cauliflower, all cooked well and full of flavor. The breads were soft, served hot, and generously buttered – the perfect partner to the gravies.

We ended our lunch with a sizzling brownie topped with vanilla ice cream. Though a few desserts we wanted weren’t available, this one made up for it. The brownie was warm, soft, and rich in chocolate flavor, pairing beautifully with the cold vanilla ice cream. Overall, while a few dishes could improve, the experience at Pali Village was very good. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Chicken_Sizzler, Sizzling_Brownie_with_Ice_Cream, Chicken_Banjara_Kebab, Chef's_Special_Chicken_Biryani, Manchow_Soup, Fried_Rice, Roti], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=It has been more than twenty years since I first visited Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar with my family, and it continues to remain a special place for us in Borivali. It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

Quantity - 4/5
Service - 4.2/5

We visited Agrezi Dhaba on Saturday, 31st May 2025, as a group of 3 married couples along with 2 kids, hoping for a pleasant evening out. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be an utter disappointment from start to finish.

First of all, imagine walking into a restaurant on a Saturday night and seeing only two waiters managing the entire floor. That alone sets the tone for what’s to come. Service was painfully slow and chaotic, with one waiter literally sprinting from table to table trying to handle everything. It felt like watching a poorly managed event, not a professional dining experience.

I had made a booking through Zomato, only to be told by the waiter that pricing would differ if we paid via the app compared to paying directly. Why play such shady pricing games with customers? This kind of misleading marketing is simply unacceptable.

To make matters worse, some of my friends ordered from the bar, only to be told they were out of Blenders Pride by 9:30 PM. On a Saturday night? That’s basic stock management gone wrong.

It was a delightful afternoon spent with great cocktails and surprising fusion of flavors and concepts. We were a party of six, so we could experience a lot on the menu and barring perhaps a couple of the dishes, every other dish was simply delectable and yum! There isn’t a “one” dish that I can single out as the highlight, there were multiple of them. Among the cocktails we tried:

·         Stranger cocktail – Refreshing and again flavor packed

On the flip side, some of the dishes in our opinion missed the mark or were simply not to our palate like the Prawn Malai Curry (felt very watery and one could only taste the galangal and not much else), Prawn Pani Puri (just felt like a bit of strange juxtaposition in terms of flavors) and the fish pulimunchi (which was good in terms of flavor but simply wasn’t pulimunchi). ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Qey - Sip & Vault in a sterling place for drink and dine Best suited for date night, group of friends, after-work drinks, stylish dinner outing. The design and interior are chic, elegant, spacious and beautiful. Music, lighting, and overall vibe are tailored for an special evening out - DJ sets, live performances are awesome. The “vault” membership concept adds a luxe, exclusive feel. The well curated menu offers European, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern fusion - chefs seem to play around with flavours and presentation - very fresh with great taste.
If you’re after a stylish evening with well-presented, flavour-forward plates rather than simple comfort food, QEY delivers. For food-centric visits, you might want to pick signature dishes in vegetarian like
• Cottage cheese kebab
• Turkish Manti
• Zaatar cottage cheese pide
• Tuscan Pici
• Taqueria bowl
• Desserts seem to leave a good mark - Salted caramel torte, Baklava cheesecake, Qey Sundae are scrumptious.
QEY has a strong focus on cocktails and a unique “sip & vault” concept: buy your bottle, store in their vault for next time. Cocktails and mocktails are beautifully crafted, perfectly balanced and unique. For cocktails and a premium bar experience, QEY hits strong. Loved its
• Grapefruit Picante
• To the Moon & Back
• Pink Coupe
• Cranberry elderflower serenade
• Summer Breeze
• Orange Chocolatini
The staff are attentive and friendly. The service is quick too. QEY is a strong choice for an upscale evening out in Lower Parel: great design + good food + standout drinks + lively ambience totally worth trying., name_person=Bhavin Parekh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=I recently visited QEY at Lower Parel (Kamala Mills), and wow — it was hands down one of the most outstanding dining experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. From the moment I walked in, the place felt grand, almost palatial: high ceilings, luxe interiors and a vibe that immediately transported me somewhere more international than local.
It was a Sunday lunch, and the light filtering through the space added a beautiful glow — calm, airy, and perfect for a relaxed, indulgent meal.
What I ate was nothing short of a feast: we went all out — there was chicken, prawns, fish and even clams. The clams especially stood out — tender, fresh and so flavourful — and the fish deserves a mention too; I’d go back just for that fish any day. Every plate arrived with such thoughtful presentation that it felt like art on a table.
We also tried a few of their cocktails — mixed live at the table — which was fun and added a playful, classy touch to the meal. And of course, I couldn’t skip dessert: I had one rich chocolate-based dessert and another creamy one — both wonderful ways to end the meal.
All in all, QEY feels like more than just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Between the ambiance, the food, the drinks, and the overall vibe, it made for a memorable outing. I’d absolutely recommend it to anyone looking for something special, and I know I’ll be back there soon., name_person=Shillpa Kataria Singh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Qey — Where the Sip & Vault concept turns dining into an experience.

Qey’s idea of Sip & Vault instantly sets it apart — it’s not just a restaurant, but a space where great conversations, inventive drinks, and artful food come together seamlessly. A very unique concept of storing your bottles in a vault makes this as a very convenient place to come again and again.

Ambience:
The space feels chic yet intimate — warm lighting, plush interiors, and a stylish crowd that gives it a cosmopolitan energy without being loud or overdone.

Food:
Every dish is thoughtfully crafted — the Mushroom Baklava is pure innovation, while the Mezze Platter is vibrant and full of character. The Harissa Spiced Chicken hits the right balance of spice and tenderness, Gambas Al Ajilo is buttery perfection, and Chicken Fricassee delivers deep, comforting flavour. The Baklava Cheesecake is a must-end — light, nutty, and indulgent.

Drinks:
The cocktail lineup truly completes the “Sip” experience — the Biscoff Royale is a decadent favourite, Pink Coupe elegant and refreshing, and Yuzu Ka bright and zesty with a creative edge.

Experience:
Qey masters the balance between concept and comfort. With its stunning design, crafted cocktails, and standout food, it’s easily one of the most well-executed new spots in town and the service fantastic

Starting off with the Cranberry Elderflower Serenade — tangy cranberry, sweet pineapple, and that hint of elderflower… fresh, floral, and just happy in a glass.

Then came the Pesto Arancini — golden, crisp on the outside, soft pesto risotto inside, and that saffron mayo steals the show.

Next, the Orange Chocolatini — citrus meets chocolate in the most indulgent way possible. Sweet, rich, and slightly zesty — absolute mood.

The Cottage Cheese Kebabs followed — smoky, creamy, perfectly spiced, sitting on that soft zaatar pita. Comfort food done right.

Cut to the Taqueria Bowl — creamy avocado hummus, tangy salsa, grilled corn, all the textures in one perfect bite.
Then Tuscan Pici — burrata, pesto, and broccoli twirling together like an Italian daydream.

And dessert? That’s where Qey goes wild.
The Enchanted Brownie Forest — gooey, nutty, straight-up chocolate heaven.
And the Qey Sundae? Brownies, berries, cookie cream — pure happiness in a bowl.

Qey proves Jain food can be fun, fancy, and full of flavor. Bookmark this spot — your next craving starts here.

But this time, the experience was honestly disappointing.

They’ve completely changed their menu, it’s now pure veg, which is fine, but the menu itself is just terrible. The pricing is extremely high, and the taste and quality don’t justify the cost at all.

The only thing I genuinely liked was the Avocado Cream Cheese Sushi, it was fresh and tasty. But again, ₹600 for just 4 pieces is definitely not okay.

We also tried the Mock Meat Nihari Biryani, and while the presentation looked great, the taste was a nightmare. The rice was super dry, the mock meat was undercooked and chewy, and to make things worse, the raita had peanut butter in it! Who even thought that was a good idea? It was honestly horrible.

Just loved how they have painted the ceiling with the map of South Mumbai and well illuminated wall depicting CSTM building structure. A nice mix of high tables, couple tables, comfortable sofa seating, regular tables and chairs section for large groups, just a very well planned layout I must say.

Talking about what all I tried here at South Bombay Bar, I actually just loved everything that was called for -

We started with few appetizers - Mexican Potatoes, Cheese Chilli Garlic Bread and Cheesy Jalapeno Stuffed Mushrooms. I just loved all three of them, but a word of caution for the Mexican Potatoes. Extremely rich in flavours but the Mexican spices also do their wonder. So it's really spicy. We actually asked the chef to tone down the spices, but we still felt it was quite spicy. So those who are in love with spice, this is your treat. I am a big fan of mushrooms and when it's jalapeno and cheese stuffing, it's heavenly. Don't miss this if you eat mushrooms. DECOR, AMBIENCE & SEATING

They have a full fledged bar which offers a wide variety of mocktails & signature cocktails to spoil you for choices.

The Bar is located in one corner, seating is spread in the middle while the DJ plays some peppy tracks on his console from the other end.

There are both indoor and outdoor seating options, including a rooftop or outdoor area with cover, which is perfect in evenings.\\n\\nThe food is mostly modern Indian with creative twists: great starters like Khow Suey Samosa, Beetroot Mozzarella Seekh, Zafrani Tangdi, and mains like Butter Chicken, Paneer Achaari, Dal Bukhara with Laccha Paratha etc.  Desserts like Gulkand Cheesecake and Matka Rabri Gulab Jamun get very good feedback.\\n\\nThe drinks/cocktails are also a highlight. Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. We were a group of 10 looking for an indulgent seafood and coastal meal in Mumbai and Coast & Bloom delivered beyond expectations. With a modern, minimalistic ambience and a menu that is curated Malvani inspirations and there were some mains like Chettinad, konkani and goan, this spot is perfect for both celebrations and leisurely meals.

What We Ordered

Our feast included a fantastic mix of seafood, meats, and sides:

- Crab Kakori

- Shallow Fried Malvani Bombil

- Chicken Chilli

- Chicken Malvani Masala

- Prawns Bhujane

- APC Pomfret & APC Crab

- Pasta Arrabiata for kids

- Rice Bhakri, Ghavane, Wade

- Solkadi

Everything was rich, flavorful, and well-prepared, especially the seafood, which was fresh and cooked to perfection.

Service Excellence

Special shout-out to Chandani, Chandan, and Roshan, they took exceptional care of us from start to finish. For a table of 10, the service was quick, warm, and always attentive. They made excellent suggestions and ensured every dietary need was handled with care.

Price & Value

Medium to high priced considering the generous portions and seafood quality. Value for money for group dining with great ambiance.

-Verdict

A must-visit for seafood lovers and anyone wanting a coastal food experience with a modern twist. The ever-popular 145 franchise has now opened its doors at Kamala Mills, adding yet another reason to visit this buzzing hub. Tucked away on the quieter back road of Kamala Mills, this outlet blends the relaxed charm of a café with the energy of a lively bar, making it a perfect pick for both day and night outings.

Pros;

1. The biggest highlight is the ambience — spacious, welcoming, and full of life. The warm colour palette, comfortable seating, and a small dance floor create just the right vibe for a good time.

2. Fresh, well-prepared food that delivers on quality every single time.

3. Generous portion sizes, ideal for sharing between two people.

4. Prompt and attentive service that keeps the experience smooth.

Cons;
None worth noting.

What we ordered;
🔸️ Ferrero Rocher Freakshake; RECOMMENDED
A chocolate lover’s dream! Thick, creamy, and indulgent, this freakshake is packed with chocolate chunks, syrup, and milk, crowned with colourful Gems and chocolate treats. Heavy and rich — perfect for serious sweet cravings.
Rating: 4/5

One of the best cranberry-based mocktails I’ve tried. Fresh cranberry juice muddled with pear, topped with ginger ale and lime — a refreshing duo that works perfectly together. A must-try for non-alcoholic drink lovers.
Rating: 4.5/5

🔸️ Chili Paneer; RECOMMENDED
A quick Chinese-style bite in a café bar setting. Soft paneer tossed with green chilies, ginger, and onions, making it a crowd-pleasing starter. Definitely worth ordering.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Jalapeño Poppers; RECOMMENDED
Golden, crispy bites filled with cheese, jalapeños, corn, and chili. A starter that’s universally loved — even better when paired with a cocktail.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Paneer Makhanwala Biryani; RECOMMENDED
A vegetarian take on the Butter Chicken Biryani we loved last time, featuring paneer tikka and a rich makhanwala gravy. While slightly on the dry side, it still stood out as a flavorful North Indian option.
Rating: 4/5

🔸️ Chicken Manchurian Fried Rice; RECOMMENDED
An all-time classic! The fried rice was well-cooked and paired with flavorful Manchurian — simple, comforting, and exactly what you’d expect.
Rating: 4/5

Final Verdict;
Every place has its strengths, and this one offers more positives than negatives. Prices are on par with most popular cafés, making it a great value for the quality and portions served. Younion season 2 is something you shouldn't miss out on.

Location: Younion is located at one of the most happening places of the town known for some really good places to hangout and night life i.e. Kamla Mills, Lower Parel.

About the Place:
A perfect place for a perfect night out along with your friends is what we would say. Younion has everything that will impress you. Each wall is beautifully decorated.   The artificial plants hanging through ceiling, nicely spaced seating arrangements, amazing music played over here and the crowd that visits this place helps to create that perfect vibe.

Younion has more than 300 shots and 25 variety of new cocktails at an affordable rates on their menu for your gang. They also have 50 new LIIT's & the menu is also made vast with more 80 dishes, largest pizza, burger & Dimsums. The food over here is also good. They have some really good fusion food perfect to have along with your drinks.

We visited this place on a Friday evening and trust us it was packed. The place is really good and the moment we entered the place we knew that we gonna spend a good time..!! The service at this place is quick and they really help you when you are confused with what to order. Kudos to Pravin for helping us with the order. We quickly ordered our drinks and food and here's what we had. Jain food is also available here.
In Drinks we tried mocktails & cocktails.
-Berry cooler, hangover, you must try this, courgae basil. Lovely drinks is what we would say.

In food we loved the
-Loaded sheet pan nachos  which was loaded with chhedar & mozzarella cheese and served with jalapeno, bell pepper & sour cream. Highly recommended.

Also not to miss out on their delicious
-Truffle shroom Burger-
Shittake mushroom, with truffle mayo & cheese. It was one of the best burger we have had in recent times. Highly Recommended..!!

Avocado green out pizza
Pizza based topped with avocado, sun-dried tomatoes, olives, parmesan & jalapenos. It was good to taste.

Furthermore we ordered spinach & cheese corn avocado tart, BBC hara bhara candy & wok tossed tofu with spinach noodles. All were delicious to taste.

We came here as my son wanted to compare the Taj, we have been to a few times, and the Oberoi. We had just watched the India Women's team face the Aussies at the Wankhede and no taxi would take us the short distance to the Oberoi so we legged it. It was nice to see Deepti Sharma picking up her keys after watching her make a 50 about 30 mins ago.

The staff welcomed us into the restaurant and we placed our orders for starters and mains. The prawn cocktail and grilled prawn starters were well presented, and cooked well but there was nothing special about their taste. Mains were the seafood risotto and the pan seared barramundi. The presentation was much to be desired from though they tasted ok but nothing special.

I would suggest the chef should spend a few weeks as a sous chef with Gordon Ramsay to learn presentation. If theu can't afford Ramsay I would suggest a week in my kitchen, in London, will definitely help them up their game.

Why I mention presentations is because Frangipani isn't inexpensive and the only reason for being inexpensive shouldn't be because they are based in the Oberoi. The chef needs to make an effort to cook and present well when they work in good quality restaurants.

Oh and did I mention that they couldn't offer us any pizza or bruschetta as the oven was broken thus further reducing the limited choice menu down., name_person=Rajesh Gosain}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 2 years ago, review=This was my first visit to this restaurant.

Upfront, I was served the bread basket having 4 varieties of bread, amongst which the red was the best. As opposed to my prima facia thought, it was neither sweet nor related to red velvet in any way.

In the main course directly, I tried a Salmon here in their default preparation, and it was very good although the sides primarily having couscous didn't taste nice. Reckon the traditional mashed potatoes would have been a better option.

I also tried another Salmon, this time specifically asking for traditional mashed potatoes at the sides, and it was given the way I would have wanted ( medium-done ) and was very good too.

The preparation time for both was c 25  mins, which is the average time for such dishes. The quantity was between small and medium when juxtaposed with the competitors.

In between, I wanted to try out an item from the buffet, a couple of cheese cuts, and the staff courteously allowed me to do so.

The mocktails were nice too despite not really corresponding to their descriptions. The first one ( orange-coloured ) ( exact name forgotten ) was quite different in taste, and on a bit thicker side. Kinda seemed like fruit juice more than the soda-based mocktail which it was ideally supposed to be. The second one viz Brazilian Virgin Mojito was the same as the normal Virgin Mojito one gets everywhere with medium power soda. I can only reasonably hunch that the prefix 'Brazil' is added to gain an attraction. Both were served within 10 mins, and the quantity was medium when juxtaposed with the competitors.

At the end, I was offered some special dark chocolates, they were delicious and I am thankful to the staff for the same.

The decor when compared to the neighbouring India Jones is not very fancy, there are about 25 tables in the restaurant which also serves the buffet and the area is quite big, and the background setting is medium ( India Jones in comparison has dim lights ). The chairs are of the same type, and at medium-level seating. The beverage menu is either not available or significantly incompletely uploaded on online food/dining sites/apps and necessary amends should be made on those respects. Also, the food menu uploaded on the food/dining app/sites is not updated, so the latest one would be appreciated.

Overall, it was a nice experience, and I will definitely visit again.

Second Visit

I began with the complimentary bread basket consisting of 4 types of bread, just like the previous visit. Coming to the main course directly, I ordered fish&chips on my second visit to this restaurant. As is the norm, it came along with French fries and tartare sauce. The tartare sauce wasn't white and not on the thick side as normally it is ( but very liquidy ), and this was the smallest quantity I had got with a fish and chips dish hitherto. However, upon asking, the staff bought another quantity of the incredibly small tartare sauce.

Mumbai's dining scene just received a stunning upgrade with the opening of Otoki at Apollo Bunder, a new sanctuary dedicated to specialty Japanese cuisine. From the moment we were settled at the intimate sushi tables, we knew we were in for a memorable experience. Otoki’s dedication to pristine ingredients and technical skill quickly turned our lunch into a true celebration of flavour, leaving us with broad smiles.

The Sublime Sushi Experience
Our focus was entirely on the raw bar, and Otoki delivered a masterclass in precision and quality. Every piece was a miniature work of art.
The Nigiri selection was flawless: the classic Bluefin Tuna Akami was pristine, and the Unagi (eel) was perfectly glazed. The Hotate (scallop) melted delicately on the tongue, but the true surprise was the Pickled Tomato nigiri—a burst of innovative, acidic freshness that elevated the traditional lineup.

The Sashimi course was a moment of sheer indulgence. The Bluefin Tuna Otoro offered that characteristic, luxurious marbling that defines perfection, dissolving on the palate with a rich, buttery texture.

The Maki rolls were meticulously crafted and perfectly balanced. We thoroughly enjoyed the traditional Norimaki, the bright, citrusy notes of the Yuzu Salmon, and the clean simplicity of the Bluefin Tuna Akami roll.

To cap off the meal, the desserts provided a sophisticated finish: the earthy sweetness of the Warabi Mochi paired perfectly with the sharp, aromatic brightness of the Yuzu Ice Cream.

Hospitality and Passion
While the food was phenomenal, the exceptional hospitality truly elevated our visit. The chefs at Otoki are a delight, well-informed, and visibly passionate about their craft.

We were fortunate enough to be looked after by Chef Yunus, who ensured we loved every bite and guided us with spot-on recommendations. He was wonderfully accompanied by Chef Rahul. Chef Yusuf, was wonderful at ensuring we were comfortable and made time for great conversations. A great host.

The entire staff is great, friendly, and contributes to the welcoming atmosphere.

Looking Ahead
Otoki currently operates a limited menu for lunch, but based on the exemplary quality we experienced, we are already counting down the days until our next visit for dinner. We look forward to being surprised with what more they have to offer.

I’ve tried Odia cuisine before, including at Orchid Hotels, but nothing really stood out back then. This place completely changed my perception of Odia food!

They offer an à la carte menu as part of the unlimited brunch, which is a refreshing concept. They also serve some snacks and sweets directly on the table. The only thing I felt was that the portion sizes are quite small, served in tiny bowls — some might find that a bit annoying, but honestly, it’s a thoughtful approach to avoid food wastage.

The non-veg dishes were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic flavours. The place also has really good vibes, and the ambiance is great for a relaxed brunch. The staff and waiters were attentive, though since it was a Sunday, the service was a little laid-back because of the crowd — but nothing that would ruin the experience.

📍 Location: Fort, Kala Ghoda
💫 Ambience: Artistic, cozy, and perfect for catching a vibe with your loved ones. The décor sets the tone for a memorable evening.

🥂 Drinks
We kicked off our evening with two standout cocktails:

Gateway Walker – Unique, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.
Bombay 01 – This one stole the show! A creative mix with bold flavors that linger.
For mocktail lovers:
Kokum Sharbat and Virgin Musketeer were both super refreshing and hit the spot!
🍽️ Starters
Kheema Mutton Pattice – Rich, flavorful, and melts in the mouth.
Taleli Kolambi – Prawns cooked in Malwani masala; absolutely mind-blowing!
Bharille Pomfret – The star of the starters! Stuffed and spiced to perfection – a must-try.
🍛 Main Course
Non-Veg Thali – A powerhouse of flavors with Kolhapuri Kombdi, Kala Mutton, Chicken Kaleji – beautifully presented and even better in taste.
Seafood Thali – Tisrya Masala, Malwani Fish Curry, Bombil Rava Fry – pure bliss for seafood lovers. Every element was top-notch.
🍮 Dessert
Ode to Puran Poli – A creative and nostalgic twist on the classic dessert. Warm, sweet, and the perfect ending to a fantastic meal.

An iconic Mumbai café with a lively vibe and historic charm. Great place to relax after Colaba Causeway shopping—food is decent, drinks are good, and the atmosphere is the real highlight.

Leopold Cafe is worth visiting for its history and energetic ambience. The food is average for the price, but the experience, crowd, and location make it a must-visit spot in South Mumbai.

Very vibrant and famous place with lots of character. Can be crowded and slightly overpriced, but still worth a visit at least once for the iconic Mumbai café experience.

📍 About the Place
Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous cafés, founded in 1871 and located on Colaba Causeway — right across from the Colaba Police Station. It’s a cultural landmark as well as a popular hangout for tourists, locals, and fans of the novel Shantaram.

The café also carries historical significance because it was one of the spots attacked during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, and some bullet marks remain preserved as a memorial.

🍽️ Ambience & Atmosphere
Vibe:
Lively, bustling, and full of character — a bit of an old-school vibe with a mix of retro and bohemian decor.

Great people-watching spot after a shopping stroll along Colaba Causeway.

Often packed, especially in evenings and weekends — queues are common

🍔 Food & Drinks — What People Say
Positives:
Wide, varied menu with continental, Indian, Chinese & bar food options.

Popular items include beer towers, shepherd’s pie, walnut pie, chocolate desserts, chicken wings, burgers and more.

Some reviewers have enjoyed refreshing drinks like Coke floats and milkshakes.

Cost:
Expect mid-range pricing — around ₹2500 for two people including drinks (approx.) with alcohol.

🧑‍🍳 Service & Crowd
What reviewers note:
✔ Friendly, helpful staff when it’s not crowded.
⚠ Can be slow or inattentive during peak hours.
⚠ Busy weekends and evenings often have lines and waiting times.

📌 Pro Tips Before You Go
This cafe is worth visiting for the experience and atmosphere, even if the food opinions vary.

Best to visit earlier in the day or on weekdays to avoid long waits.

Guests seated near windows often enjoy partial views of the waterfront or Gateway, enhancing the ambiance.  ￼

Just loved each of them. Plus the view surely looks amazing.

Wonderful service Too., name_person=Prashant}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=First, yes it is expensive. Second, service is very good, attentive and knowledgeable. A great experience., name_person=Saurabh Lal}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=8 years ago, review=My first real introduction to Japanese food. I am so glad we came here instead of going to my favourite Italian restaurant...
We had sushi and a sort of white asparagus (you can tell I am a total newbie) with a really delicious gravy.
A salad that the chef had made for the president of the US (I added mushrooms and it tasted Divine)... Am sure the president didn't get mushrooms with his salad.
They surprised us with a totally decadent rich dark chocolate cake with hints of raspberry in it. It was my birthday and this was a brilliant lunch.
We sat by the window and we should have had a view of the sea... But the building was undergoing construction so that was obscured.
The music was horrible and they did shut it off for a few minutes when we requested... But put it back on...
That was the only thing that spoilt a lovely afternoon out... But the food was so good, I couldn't give them a 4 star rating. It has to be a full 5!
Am I coming back here? Yes. Most definitely!, name_person=Khurshed Batliwala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 2 years ago, review=One of the best Japanese restaurants in town although a little overpriced. Its a must try but only a once try kind of a restaurant. Except the rock shrimp tempura which wasn't that great in terms of taste none of the dishes justify their price when it comes to the portion or the lack of it. The spicy angel shrimp sushi which is their take on prawn tempura sushi with a different sauce which came recommended by the server is a must try but the portion is a little underwhelming. The king crab robatayaki was good but neither the the taste nor the portion justify the price. The dessert which again came recommended by the server was the highlight of the night. I would recommend going to the restaurant even if its just to try the dessert., name_person=Shubham Deshpande}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Fantastic japanese cuisine with service to back it up. The chefs are well trained and masters at what they do as is evident by the presentation and detail. Fresh wasabi is quite rare at a Japanese restaurant but it’s served here fresh at your table side, ground on shark skin as is traditional. I would stay away from saucy dishes and just focus on the fish and rice and never be dissapointed here., name_person=Dan Moodley}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+}, time_line=3 years ago, review=After reading many good reviews and recommendations, we came to Wasabi with very high expectations, but the whole dinning experience was very disappointing, I suggest if you are Asian or foodie who has been to other countries and tried Japanese food, don't waste your money here.
We ordered 2 non-veg omasake, 2 soft beverages, 1 appetizer and 1 sushi, combination of omasake was a tragedy— heavy appetizers, everything was dipped in strong sauce, mayonnaise and Jalapeños on top, after thick starters they served light flavor nigiri sushi— your palate are already tired at this time, the mushroom rice and dessert are ok, but can't smooth our bad feeling, it’s the fusion Japanese cuisine that caters to foreigner taste, the whole dinner cost around INR 25,000, you will definitely have better options in Mumbai, especially Mumbai has bunch of fresh seafood can choose. Enjoying the Henri Bou…, name_person=Shailendra Mishra}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great place and seating arrangement is good staff and service also very good}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Interior of restaurant makes you feel welcome and try new tasty Japanese dishes.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Prices were a bit high but worth it for the quality of the food and experience.}"]

I would say the mocktails were good, the sea bass(from robatayaki) was good, but everything else was average. We asked the waiter what they’re known for, and they said sushi and robatayaki. The sushi was okay, but expected better for that price point. I’ve had sushi all over the world and this was just average. We ordered the coconut crab salad, it was terrible and not what we expected. We barely touched it and the waiter did not even care to ask about it.
Truly astonishing for a high end restaurant at a high end hotel to provide that level of service.
This place is definitely overhyped, the 4.9 rating is underwhelming. The expensive price is not worth the taste at all. For that same price elsewhere, I would have gotten a great experience, and trust me when I say that because I’ve been to a lot of high end restaurants.
Maybe the Indian food would have been better, but don’t recommend sushi if that’s not what you’re best at.

Taj Mahal Palace is far better in food, service and value., name_person=Dr Neelam Prakash Bandivadekar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=Visiting Mumbai from CA after a long time and looking forward to eating at Ziya Oberoi. Sadly it's still undergoing renovation and hotel invited us to eat at Fenix, which was serving some Ziya dishes.

This was our experience on Oct 21.

From the Ziya page, we ordered the Nawab Chicken starter, which turned out to be quite bland but inoffensive.

Mains were Tadka Dahi Baigan and Ghee Roast Lamb. I suppose if you like your dish drowning and overpowered by dahi, then you'll like the baigan. I must say it was disappointing for us so we ate around the sauce. The lamb was rich and flavorful so 1 out of 3 could be called success!

The reason for the low score on service was entirely due to this. I always have a blended whisky on ice with Indian food.  It complements the flavors and doesn't bloat you like beer does. No need to waste a single malt if you're going to dump ice into it. So imagine my surprise when  the bill arrived and I was charged for a Glenlivet 12 instead of Chivas 12, which is what I asked for. This was INR 300 more expensive per shot and I had 2 doubles. When I asked if they had made a mistake, I was told that they accidentally served me the Glenlivet and the bill would remain unchanged. I'm only thankful they didnt "accidentally" serve and charge me for Johnny W Blue!!

At the end of the day, it's only INR 1200 ($14) more but the least I would expected is for Fenix to just charge me for what I ordered rather than what they served! Total bill for 2 was nearly INR 16 000 and we came away thinking maybe fine Indian dining in India is not worth it. Best to eat where the locals do.

My advice, if you want top and Indian cuisine, then go to London!, name_person=Harminder Sehmi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=a year ago, review=We had an EPIC dinner evening with our family of 5.
